messages:
eli: heads-up — hitting a weird embeddings/rerank parity snag between the Node sampleapp and the python one. Node sends a batch of 3 vectors, server replies with 'vector length mismatch: expected 1024 got 1023' and then our client retries the whole batch which duplicates calls. repro attached below.

eli: request body (trimmed):
```
{
  model: 'redwood-embed-001',
  inputs: [vec1, vec2, vec3],
  // each vec is a float32 array, length supposedly 1024
} 
```

eli: headers: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
eli: logs: `400 vector-length-mismatch -> client retry -> 202 queued -> duplicate embeddings observed`

maria: can you paste one of the actual vectors (len 1023 vs 1024)? suspicious our JS batch helper might be slicing incorrectly when concatenating Float32Arrays. :thinking_face: 

eli: pasted a small repro below (node):
```js
// sample snippet from batch helper
const buf = Buffer.concat(vectors.map(v => Buffer.from(new Float32Array(v).buffer)));
const body = { inputs: splitFromBuffer(buf) }; // splitFromBuffer tries to chunk by (len * 4) bytes
```
eli: i think the math for chunk sizes was off-by-1 when last vector length % 4 != 0 in some cases (python path never hit it).

sam: hmm — also check encoding vs endianness? Node Buffer.from(Float32Array.buffer) should be LE by default but if any upstream rounding trimmed trailing zeros it could change byte length.

sam: quick workaround: validate vector.length === expectedDim before sending and log + drop/patch if not.

jasper: agreed we should add a client-side guard in both SDKs. we had a similar PR for sequence batching ages ago. i'll open a small patch in the JS SDK that rejects requests with mismatched dims and surface a clear error instead of letting the request go and trigger retry loops.

eli: that'd prevent the confusing 400->retry loop. currently retry policy treats 4xx as retryable in the sampleapp wrapper (we did this to be resilient for transient auth flaps).

maria: oof — 4xx retry policy is too broad. we should special-case vector-length-mismatch and auth 401,429 only for backoff. i'll add a tiny rule in sampleapp middleware.

eli: temporary local fix i used: padVectors(vecs, expectedDim) — pads with zeros when short. works for my test but probably hides bugs.

jasper: pad is fine as a stopgap but SDK should not silently change client data without opt-in. i'll add `validateVectors` config with `mode: 'strict'|'pad'|'truncate'`.

sam: also noticed the response format from rerank differs: python returns `id` on each embedding, node path returned array with no ids in one run. we should align the SDK response wrapper to always attach an id (index or provided). file an issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/453

ci-bot: PR opened by jasper: https://github.com/redwood-inference/js-sdk/pull/782 — "validate vector dims before send; expose pad/truncate options" :white_check_mark:

maria: can we add an integration test in sampleapp that runs a tiny Node + Python embed flow and compares outputs to catch parity regressions? add to CI matrix, run on pull.

jasper: adding test now. will also include a small fuzz of trailing zeros/odd-lengthed buffers.

sam: note for ops — this bug can create duplicate billing if retry loops double-submit batches. flagging for finance FYI. :money_with_wings: 

eli: thanks all. i'll keep this thread updated with the sampleapp repro link and a minimal failing gist. appreciate the quick triage. :rocket:
